newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share prices down in slow market.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share prices down in slow market.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped on Monday in slow trading dominated by a cotton ginning firm and two banks.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 0.06 points lower at 349.8 points in below-average turnover of 48.40 million pounds ($14.3 million).

"The market is slipping as institutional investors are taking advantage of uneducated investors. I am very optimistic for the next few weeks though. The CMA are working on a new trading system which should help," said Mohammed Abdullah, managing director of Intercapital brokerage.
Nile Cotton Ginning was the day's most active share, trading in 4.25 million pounds in what appeared to be a private deal, but it ended unchanged at 54 pounds.
"Nile Cotton has very high assets but its operations are not very good," said Abdullah.
The Egyptian state sold 2.896 million shares, or more than 48 percent, of Nile Cotton Ginning to strategic investors in February.
The banking sector again performed well. Egyptian American Bank/EAB and Commercial International Bank/CIB together traded in shares worth almost eight million pounds.
EAB offered investors 1.2 million shares or 10 percent of the bank's equity at a starting price of 127 pounds from July 2.
The bank closed 2.25 higher at 126 after trading in 3.7 million pounds.

"It's getting close to the closing date of the sale. There is some demand because it has closed lower than the minimum starting price and the bank will soon distribute a coupon of six pounds," said Abdullah.
CIB slipped 0.35 pounds to 72.1 after trading in shares worth four million pounds.
"Trade is picking up after Salomon Brothers said CIB was a strong buy," Abdullah said. Salomon Brothers gave a "strong buy" recommendation to CIB in an equity research report.

Other active shares included Alexandria National Iron and Steel (ANSDK) which traded a healthy 3.2 million pounds and ended almost unchanged at 238.99, and al-Ahram Beverages Company,, or Pyramids Breweries, which rose one pound to 129 after trading in 2.2 million pounds.
North Cairo Flour Mills jumped three pounds to 184, making the most active share in Monday's milling sector.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 473.57 points from 473.52 points while that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 260.19 from 260.27.
Of the 88 shares traded, 27 rose, 40 fell while 21 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
